answer.location_description: Horizontal band across the full width of the top edge of the image (rows 0-3), away from the central nodule.
answer.shortcut_type: bright band/strip artifact along the top image border
answer.mechanism: Layer-1 unit 23 (bias +26, so usually active) is a top-band detector. Its layer-2 weights mostly feed benign-leaning paths: u8 (+92, output weight -43), u1 (+76, output -79), u14 (-80, output +91, the strongest malignant unit) and u3 (-80, output +53). Bright pixels in rows 0-3 therefore lower the logit. Unit 17 (positive on the top and bottom rows, negative in the centre) adds a weaker benign push.
answer.evidence: Unit 23's weights in rows 0-3 are almost all large positives (e.g. r0: 80, 86, 79, 80, 89; r1: 84, 65, 68, 85, 80, 84; r3: 87, 69, 70, 74, 70, 75, 73, 81), several above the roughly ±80 range of the untrained-looking units. From row 4 down its weights look like noise. No other unit has a strong edge-localized pattern like this; the other trained units (1, 8, 18, 20, 29) are centred on the nodule. Summing w2×w3 over the layer-2 units, unit 23's net effect on the logit is negative (about -6000 in integer-product units, and more negative if the low-bias unit u15 is off). Caveat: unit 23 also leans positive along columns 0-1, unit 17 is not top-specific, and a top-edge band could be anatomy such as chest wall, so this call is only moderately confident.
answer.main_feature: Brightness and extent of tissue in the central region (roughly rows 5-19, cols 4-19), i.e. nodule size and density. Units 8, 18, 20 and 1 have centred positive weights whose pathways strongly raise the malignant logit, so larger or denser central nodules are scored as malignant.
